summary: The K-ETA portal lists the countries and regions whose passport holders can apply for K-ETA, with each one's allowed period of stay; it says nationals eligible for K-ETA who wish to enter without a visa must obtain K-ETA approval before boarding, for a fee of 10,000 KRW, and that a K-ETA is valid for 3 years. The Ministry of Justice has extended a temporary K-ETA exemption to December 31, 2026 for the countries and regions currently exempt; Korea's foreign ministry listed 22 of them, including the US, UK and Japan. Korea's visa portal says visa application centres receive visa applications on behalf of embassies and consulates.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or K-ETA for South Korea?
faq.answer: The K-ETA portal lists the United States of America with an allowed period of stay of 90 days. A K-ETA is normally required before boarding, but the United States was among the 22 countries/regions Korea's foreign ministry listed for the temporary K-ETA exemption, and the Ministry of Justice has extended the exemption to December 31, 2026 for the countries currently exempt.

faq.question: What is the K-ETA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The K-ETA portal says nationals eligible for K-ETA who wish to enter without a visa must obtain approval before boarding the flight or ship. The fee is 10,000 KRW (approximately USD 7–8), plus an online payment processing fee of generally about 3%, and is non-refundable. Assessment typically takes 72 hours or less, the K-ETA can be used multiple times within its 3-year validity, and holders are exempt from submitting the arrival card.

faq.question: How long can Canadians stay in South Korea?
faq.answer: The K-ETA portal lists Canada with an allowed period of stay of 6 months. Canada was among the 22 countries/regions Korea's foreign ministry listed for the temporary K-ETA exemption, which the Ministry of Justice has extended to December 31, 2026 for the countries currently exempt.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit South Korea without a visa?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Justice says that in Jeju Special Self-Governing Province Chinese nationals may, as before, stay visa-free for 30 days, travelling individually or in groups. It announced a temporary visa-free scheme for Chinese tour groups of three or more recruited by designated travel agencies, for stays of up to 15 days anywhere in Korea, from 29 September 2025 to 30 June 2026. No official source we could read states an extension.

faq.question: How much does a South Korean tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: Article 71 of the Enforcement Rules of the Immigration Act sets the visa fee at the equivalent of USD 40 for a single-entry visa for a stay of up to 90 days, USD 60 for 91 days or more, USD 70 for a double-entry visa and USD 90 for an unlimited multiple-entry visa; heads of missions collecting it in local currency set the base amount taking exchange rates into account. Korea's visa portal says visa application centres receive applications and hand over visas on behalf of embassies and consulates.
